literal: Wealth having destroyed, falsehood having adopted, grace having destroyed, misery causing to suffer, gambling.
translation: Gambling destroys one's wealth, drives them to adopt falsehood, ruins their compassion, and plunges them into endless misery.
modern: சூதாட்டம் ஒருவனுடைய செல்வத்தை அழித்து, அவனைப் பொய் சொல்ல வைத்து, அவனுடைய இரக்க குணத்தையும் அழித்து, துன்பத்தில் உழலச் செய்யும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the destructive path of gambling on a person's life and character. First, it ruins their material wealth (poruḷ). To sustain the habit or cover losses, the gambler is forced to adopt falsehood (poy) and deceit. This moral decline eventually destroys their innate sense of grace and compassion (aruḷ) for others. Ultimately, the vice of gambling (cūtu) leaves the individual trapped in a state of perpetual suffering and misery (allal).
